docs.title: Cortex — Overview
docs.text: Cortex (v2.0.0) is a personal knowledge management MCP server that lets you capture, search, and synthesise information across two distinct stores. It runs over stdio transport, uses Supabase for vector embeddings, and exposes its full surface through MCP tools.

docs.title: Thoughts Store
docs.text:
Thoughts are atomic, source-agnostic entries. When you capture a thought, Cortex automatically embeds it and extracts structured metadata — topics, type classification, people mentioned, and action items. Thoughts can originate from any source: direct MCP capture, web ingestion, or Discord. They are designed to be ephemeral working memory: low friction to create, fast to search by meaning, and filterable by type, topic, person, or recency.

Thought types: observation, task, idea, reference, person_note

docs.title: WikiVault Store
docs.text:
WikiVault pages are durable, structured markdown files with auto-generated frontmatter. They are LLM-maintained — intended to be created and updated by an AI agent synthesising information from Thoughts and raw sources. Pages live in typed subfolders and are indexed in Supabase alongside their embeddings.

Wiki types (curated knowledge):

Type Purpose wiki_person Profile pages for people wiki_project Project summaries and status wiki_concept Concept definitions and explanations wiki_area Broad life/work area overviews wiki_topic Topic-level knowledge aggregations

Raw types (imported source material):

Type Purpose raw_article Articles imported from MainVault or web raw_book Book notes and highlights raw_daily Daily notes raw_attachment Supporting files and attachments

docs.title: 1. Thought Capture & Browsing
docs.text: Save atomic notes with capture_thought. Metadata extraction is automatic — you supply only the content. Browse what you've captured chronologically with list_thoughts, or get an aggregate summary via thought_stats.

docs.title: 2. Semantic Search
docs.text:
Find content by meaning, not just keywords. Cortex provides scoped and combined search:

  • search_thoughts — thoughts only
  • search_wiki — WikiVault pages only, with optional type filter
  • search_messages — past AI chat conversation history
  • search_all — all stores simultaneously; results tagged [thought] or [wiki]

All semantic search tools use configurable similarity thresholds and result limits.

docs.title: 3. Wiki Authoring
docs.text:
Create and maintain structured knowledge pages with a strict read-before-write protocol:

  1. read_wiki_page — always call this first if the page may exist
  2. write_wiki_page — create or overwrite with merged content
  3. append_wiki_log — record what was done in log.md

list_wiki_pages lets you enumerate all pages of a given type without reading their bodies, using a filesystem scan that requires no database.

docs.title: 4. Vault Migration
docs.text: migrate_vault_file imports individual files or batch-migrates from a legacy MainVault into WikiVault's raw/ subfolders. It adds standardised frontmatter, strips Dataview blocks, embeds the content, and indexes it in Supabase — without modifying the original source file.

docs.title: Capture → Search → Synthesise
docs.text:
1. capture_thought        — save an insight or observation
2. search_thoughts        — resurface relevant past thoughts by meaning
   OR search_all          — cast a wider net across thoughts + wiki
3. read_wiki_page         — check whether a synthesis page already exists
4. write_wiki_page        — create or update the wiki page with synthesised content
5. append_wiki_log        — record the action taken

docs.title: Import → Discover → Reference
docs.text:
1. migrate_vault_file     — import a legacy article or book note into raw/
2. search_wiki            — find the imported page by meaning
3. write_wiki_page        — create a wiki page that lists it as a page_source
4. append_wiki_log        — record the new page and its sources

docs.title: Daily Review
docs.text:
1. list_thoughts          — browse recent captures (filter by days=1 or days=7)
2. thought_stats          — see type and topic distribution across all captures
3. search_messages        — find relevant things discussed in past AI sessions
4. write_wiki_page        — update a person or project page with new information

docs.title: Architecture Notes
docs.text:
• Transport: stdio — Cortex runs as a subprocess, communicating over standard input/output.
  • Vector store: Supabase stores embeddings for both Thoughts and WikiVault pages, enabling semantic similarity search across all content.
  • Auto-embedding: Both capture_thought and write_wiki_page automatically generate and store embeddings on write — no separate indexing step required.
  • Frontmatter management: write_wiki_page builds frontmatter automatically from structured parameters. Do not include frontmatter in the body parameter.
  • Read-before-write enforcement: write_wiki_page performs a full overwrite. Always call read_wiki_page first when a page might already contain content, merge your changes, then write the combined result.
  • Audit trail: append_wiki_log appends to a single log.md file in WikiVault. Call it after every write_wiki_page or significant decision to maintain a recoverable history of changes.

docs.title: Thought Capture & Browsing
docs.text: Tool Description capture_thought Save a new note with automatic metadata extraction (topics, type, people, action items) list_thoughts Browse recently captured thoughts with optional filters for type, topic, person, and recency thought_stats Get summary counts and breakdowns: total thoughts, type distribution, top topics and people

docs.title: Semantic Search
docs.text: Tool Description search_thoughts Semantic search over captured thoughts only search_messages Semantic search over past AI chat conversation messages search_wiki Semantic search over WikiVault pages, with optional type filter search_all Unified semantic search across all stores (thoughts + wiki pages); results tagged by source

docs.title: Wiki Authoring
docs.text: Tool Description write_wiki_page Create or overwrite a WikiVault page; auto-builds frontmatter and indexes content read_wiki_page Read full body and frontmatter of a WikiVault page by title or file path list_wiki_pages Browse wiki pages by type or tag via filesystem scan; returns titles, types, tags, paths — no bodies append_wiki_log Write a one-line audit log entry to log.md after any write action

docs.title: Vault Migration
docs.text: Tool Description migrate_vault_file One-time import of a MainVault file into WikiVault raw/; normalizes frontmatter, strips Dataview blocks, embeds, and indexes

docs.title: Choosing the Right Search Tool
docs.text:
Goal Use Search captured notes and thoughts only search_thoughts Search past AI chat conversations search_messages Search wiki pages only (people, projects, concepts, etc.) search_wiki Broadest search / unknown which store holds the information search_all

search_all has a lower default threshold (0.45 vs 0.5) and returns results tagged [thought] or [wiki] so you can distinguish sources.

docs.title: Choosing the Right Write Tool
docs.text: Goal Use Save an atomic note, insight, decision, or task capture_thought Create or update a structured wiki page (person, project, concept, area, topic) read_wiki_page → write_wiki_page Import a legacy file from MainVault into WikiVault raw/ migrate_vault_file

docs.title: Read-Before-Write Protocol
docs.text:
Never call write_wiki_page on a page that may already exist without first reading it. Follow these steps:

  1. Call read_wiki_page with the target page title or relative file path.
  2. Inspect the returned body and frontmatter for existing content, tags, sources, and status.
  3. Merge or update content as needed — preserving information you are not explicitly replacing.
  4. Call write_wiki_page with the full revised body (including all retained content).
  5. Call append_wiki_log with the file path and a one-line summary of what was changed.

Skipping step 1 risks silently clobbering existing knowledge. write_wiki_page performs a full overwrite — there is no partial-update operation.

docs.title: append_wiki_log
docs.text:
Writes a single timestamped line to log.md in WikiVault documenting an action that was taken. This is the sole mechanism for maintaining an audit trail of all wiki mutations.

Call this tool after every write_wiki_page call and after any other significant decision affecting the wiki. Skipping it breaks log continuity and makes the change history unreliable.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description file_path string ✅ Yes — Relative path of the page that was acted on (e.g. wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md) summary string ✅ Yes — One-line description of what was done. Maximum 200 characters.

docs.title: Parameter notes
docs.text:
• file_path should be the relative path within WikiVault, matching the path returned by write_wiki_page or visible in list_wiki_pages results. Use the canonical path, not an alias or title string.
  • summary must be concise and self-contained. It should describe what changed and why in enough detail that someone reading log.md weeks later can understand the action without context. Hard limit: 200 characters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Confirmation that the log entry was written to log.md, including the timestamp applied to the entry.

docs.title: When to call
docs.text: Trigger Required? After write_wiki_page (create or overwrite) ✅ Always After any significant decision about wiki structure ✅ Yes After migrate_vault_file ✅ Yes After a read-only operation (read_wiki_page, search_wiki, list_wiki_pages) ❌ No

docs.title: Basic: logging a page update
docs.text:
{
  "file_path": "wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md",
  "summary": "Added Q3 promotion note and updated role to Staff Engineer"
}

docs.title: Logging a new page creation
docs.text:
{
  "file_path": "wiki/projects/Project-Phoenix.md",
  "summary": "Created new project page synthesising 4 captured thoughts from discovery phase"
}

docs.title: Logging a migration
docs.text:
{
  "file_path": "raw/articles/notes-on-distributed-systems.md",
  "summary": "Migrated from MainVault; stripped Dataview blocks; indexed in Supabase"
}

docs.title: Typical write sequence
docs.text:
Every wiki write operation should follow this three-step pattern:

  1. read_wiki_page — read current content to avoid clobbering
  2. write_wiki_page — write the updated content
  3. append_wiki_log — record what was done
// Step 3 — called immediately after write_wiki_page succeeds
{
  "file_path": "wiki/concepts/Second-Brain.md",
  "summary": "Expanded definition section; linked to new wiki/projects/Cortex-Setup.md"
}

docs.title: Audit trail behaviour
docs.text:
• All entries are appended to a single log.md file at the root of WikiVault.
  • Each entry is automatically timestamped by the server at the moment of the call.
  • Entries are append-only — append_wiki_log never modifies or deletes existing log lines.
  • The log is human-readable and can be reviewed directly in any markdown viewer.

docs.title: capture_thought
docs.text: Save a new note or thought to Cortex. Automatically embeds and extracts metadata (topics, type, people, action items). Use when the user wants to save an insight, decision, observation, or task.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description content string Yes — The thought to capture — a clear, self-contained statement

docs.title: content guidance
docs.text: Write content as a complete, standalone statement that will make sense when read back later without surrounding context. Include relevant names, project references, and decisions inline. A vague fragment like "discussed auth" is less useful than "Decided to migrate the auth service to OAuth 2.0 by end of Q3 — owner: Alice Smith".

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: The tool returns a confirmation that the thought was saved, along with the extracted metadata Cortex derived automatically — which may include the inferred thought type, topics, people mentioned, and any action items detected in the content. The exact shape of the returned object is determined by the server at runtime.

docs.title: When to use
docs.text:
• The user explicitly asks to save, capture, note, or remember something.
  • An important insight, decision, or task surfaces during a conversation that should be persisted beyond the current session.
  • You want to create a record that can later be retrieved via search_thoughts, list_thoughts, or thought_stats.

docs.title: Capture a decision
docs.text:
{
  "content": "Decided to migrate the auth service to OAuth 2.0 by end of Q3 — owner: Alice Smith"
}

Cortex will automatically extract topics (e.g. auth, oauth), identify Alice Smith as a person mentioned, and classify the thought type based on the content.

docs.title: Capture an observation
docs.text:
{
  "content": "The onboarding funnel drop-off rate spiked 12% after the v2.4 release — likely caused by the new email verification step"
}

docs.title: Capture a task
docs.text:
{
  "content": "Follow up with the infrastructure team about the load balancer timeout settings before the next deploy"
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Pass the full context in content — Cortex uses the text itself to generate the embedding and infer metadata, so richer input produces more useful extraction and retrieval.
  • There is no separate type or topic parameter on this tool; all classification is derived automatically from the content string.
  • After capturing, use search_thoughts to verify the thought is retrievable by meaning, or list_thoughts to browse recent entries chronologically.

docs.title: list_thoughts
docs.text:
Browse recently captured thoughts with optional filters. Use this tool when you want a list of thoughts rather than a semantic search — for example, to audit recent captures, review open tasks, or see what was noted about a specific person or topic.

All parameters are optional. Omit all of them to retrieve the most recently captured thoughts up to the default limit.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description limit number No 10 Maximum number of results to return. type string No — Filter by thought type. Accepted values: observation, task, idea, reference, person_note. topic string No — Filter by topic tag. person string No — Filter by person mentioned. days number No — Restrict results to thoughts captured within the last N days.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: An ordered list of thought entries matching the supplied filters. Each entry includes the thought's content, metadata, and timestamp. No filters applied returns up to limit thoughts.

docs.title: Browse recent thoughts (no filters)
docs.text:
{
  "tool": "list_thoughts",
  "params": {}
}

Returns up to 10 recently captured thoughts.

docs.title: List all captured tasks
docs.text:
{
  "tool": "list_thoughts",
  "params": {
    "type": "task"
  }
}

docs.title: Tasks mentioning Alice Smith from the last 7 days
docs.text:
{
  "tool": "list_thoughts",
  "params": {
    "type": "task",
    "person": "Alice Smith",
    "days": 7
  }
}

Returns task-type thoughts that mention Alice Smith and were captured within the last 7 days.

docs.title: Ideas tagged with a specific topic, larger result set
docs.text:
{
  "tool": "list_thoughts",
  "params": {
    "type": "idea",
    "topic": "product-strategy",
    "limit": 25
  }
}

docs.title: Recent observations (last 3 days)
docs.text:
{
  "tool": "list_thoughts",
  "params": {
    "type": "observation",
    "days": 3
  }
}

docs.title: When to use list_thoughts vs. other tools
docs.text: Goal Recommended tool Browse or audit recent captures by recency list_thoughts Find thoughts by meaning or topic without knowing exact tags search_thoughts Search across both thoughts and wiki pages search_all Get aggregate counts and breakdowns thought_stats

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• All parameters are optional and combinable — supply any combination of type, topic, person, and days to narrow results.
  • When no filters are provided, results are limited to limit entries (default 10).
  • Use search_thoughts if you want to find thoughts by semantic similarity rather than by explicit metadata filters.

docs.title: list_wiki_pages
docs.text:
Browse WikiVault pages with optional filters. Returns title, type, tags, and file path for each matching page — no page bodies. Operates via filesystem scan, so it works without a Supabase/DB connection.

Use this tool for enumeration tasks — listing all pages of a given type, finding all pages with a specific tag, or auditing coverage. For meaning-based discovery (e.g. "pages about machine learning"), use search_wiki instead.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description type string (enum) No — Filter results to one page type. See valid values below. tag string No — Filter by a single tag. limit number No 50 Maximum number of results to return.

docs.title: Valid type values
docs.text:
Value Description wiki_person Person profile pages wiki_project Project pages wiki_concept Concept or idea pages wiki_area Area-of-responsibility pages wiki_topic Topic overview pages raw_article Imported article content raw_book Imported book notes raw_daily Daily note entries raw_attachment Attachment files

All parameters are optional. Calling list_wiki_pages with no arguments returns up to 50 pages across all types.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A list of matching pages. Each result includes:

  • title — the human-readable page title
  • type — the page type (one of the enum values above)
  • tags — array of tags associated with the page
  • file path — the relative path to the page file in WikiVault

No page bodies are returned. To read a page's full content, pass its title or file path to read_wiki_page.

docs.title: List all person pages
docs.text:
{
  "type": "wiki_person"
}

docs.title: List all pages tagged "engineering"
docs.text:
{
  "tag": "engineering"
}

docs.title: List person pages tagged "engineering"
docs.text:
{
  "type": "wiki_person",
  "tag": "engineering"
}

Returns all wiki_person pages that carry the engineering tag — useful for auditing which engineers have wiki entries.

docs.title: List all pages, increased limit
docs.text:
{
  "limit": 100
}

docs.title: List raw articles, capped at 20
docs.text:
{
  "type": "raw_article",
  "limit": 20
}

docs.title: When to Use This Tool
docs.text: Goal Tool List all pages of a given type list_wiki_pages with type Find pages with a specific tag list_wiki_pages with tag Find pages by meaning or topic search_wiki Read a specific page's content read_wiki_page Search thoughts and wiki together search_all

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Results are limited to metadata only. The tool does not return page bodies, so follow up with read_wiki_page for full content.
  • type and tag filters are independent and can be combined. When both are provided, results must satisfy both conditions.
  • Because this tool scans the filesystem rather than querying the database, it reflects the current state of files on disk and does not require Supabase to be available.

docs.title: migrate_vault_file
docs.text:
Copies a file from MainVault into the WikiVault raw/ folder, applies standardised frontmatter, strips Dataview blocks, generates vector embeddings, and indexes the result in Supabase. The original MainVault source file is never modified.

Use this tool during a one-time vault migration or to import individual articles on demand. It is scoped to raw_* page types only — for managed wiki entries (wiki_person, wiki_project, etc.), use write_wiki_page instead.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description source_path string Yes — Absolute path to the MainVault source file, e.g. /Users/me/MainVault/Articles/transformer-paper.md target_type string (enum) Yes — Destination subfolder type. One of: raw_article, raw_book, raw_daily, raw_attachment force boolean No false If true, overwrites an existing WikiVault file at the computed target path

docs.title: target_type values
docs.text:
Value Description raw_article An article or essay imported from MainVault raw_book A book note or summary raw_daily A daily note raw_attachment An attachment or supporting file

The exact destination path within raw/ is determined by the server based on target_type.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: On success, returns a confirmation that includes the relative path of the newly created WikiVault file and a summary of the transformations applied (frontmatter added, Dataview blocks stripped, embedding stored, Supabase index entry created). The exact response structure is server-defined.

docs.title: Behaviour notes
docs.text:
• Non-destructive: the original MainVault file is never modified or deleted.
  • Dataview stripping: Dataview query blocks in the source are removed before the file is written to WikiVault.
  • Frontmatter: standardised frontmatter is added to the WikiVault copy automatically; you do not need to supply it.
  • Embedding + indexing: the imported file is embedded and indexed in Supabase so it is immediately searchable via search_wiki and search_all.
  • Overwrite guard: if the target file already exists in WikiVault and force is false, the tool will not overwrite it. Set force: true to replace an existing file.

docs.title: Import a single article
docs.text:
{
  "name": "migrate_vault_file",
  "arguments": {
    "source_path": "/Users/me/MainVault/Articles/transformer-paper.md",
    "target_type": "raw_article",
    "force": false
  }
}

docs.title: Re-import a book note, replacing any existing copy
docs.text:
{
  "name": "migrate_vault_file",
  "arguments": {
    "source_path": "/Users/me/MainVault/Books/thinking-fast-and-slow.md",
    "target_type": "raw_book",
    "force": true
  }
}

docs.title: Import a daily note
docs.text:
{
  "name": "migrate_vault_file",
  "arguments": {
    "source_path": "/Users/me/MainVault/Daily/2024-01-15.md",
    "target_type": "raw_daily"
  }
}

docs.title: When to use this tool
docs.text:
• Bulk migration: iterating over MainVault files and importing them into WikiVault in a single pass.
  • On-demand import: a specific source file needs to be made searchable in WikiVault without manually rewriting it.
  • Re-indexing: a previously imported file has changed in MainVault and needs to be reimported with force: true.

Do not use migrate_vault_file for: - Creating or updating managed wiki pages — use write_wiki_page for those. - Files you have already written directly into WikiVault via write_wiki_page.

docs.title: read_wiki_page
docs.text: Read the full content and frontmatter of a WikiVault page by title or relative file path. Always call this before write_wiki_page if the page may already exist — never overwrite content you have not read.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description identifier string Yes — Page title (e.g. "Alice Smith") or relative file path (e.g. "wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md")

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
The complete page content: parsed frontmatter fields and the full markdown body. The exact shape of the returned object depends on what frontmatter the page contains — fields present will reflect what was written when the page was created or last updated via write_wiki_page.

If the page does not exist, the tool returns an error response. Receiving a not-found error confirms that no page exists at that identifier, and it is safe to proceed with creating a new page via write_wiki_page.

docs.title: Read-before-write protocol
docs.text:
read_wiki_page is the mandatory first step whenever a page might already exist:

  1. Call read_wiki_page with the page title or path.
  2. If the page exists, inspect its current body and frontmatter.
  3. Merge or update the content as needed.
  4. Call write_wiki_page with the merged result.
  5. Call append_wiki_log to record the change.

Skipping step 1 risks silently clobbering existing content.

docs.title: Look up by title
docs.text:
{
  "identifier": "Alice Smith"
}

docs.title: Look up by relative file path
docs.text:
{
  "identifier": "wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md"
}

docs.title: Read-then-write workflow
docs.text:
// Step 1 — read the existing page
{
  "tool": "read_wiki_page",
  "params": { "identifier": "Alice Smith" }
}

// Step 2 — the response contains the current frontmatter and body.
// Merge new information into the body.

// Step 3 — write the updated page back
{
  "tool": "write_wiki_page",
  "params": {
    "title": "Alice Smith",
    "type": "wiki_person",
    "body": "<existing body with new information merged in>"
  }
}

// Step 4 — log the change
{
  "tool": "append_wiki_log",
  "params": {
    "file_path": "wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md",
    "summary": "Added new project context to Alice Smith page"
  }
}

docs.title: Related tools
docs.text: Tool When to use write_wiki_page Create or overwrite a page — always preceded by read_wiki_page if the page may exist search_wiki Find pages by semantic similarity when you do not know the exact title or path list_wiki_pages Browse all pages of a given type to discover titles and paths append_wiki_log Record an audit entry after every write

docs.title: search_all
docs.text:
Performs a unified semantic search across all Cortex stores at once: captured thoughts (from web, Discord, and MCP capture) and WikiVault pages. Results are returned as a single merged, ranked list with each item tagged [thought] or [wiki] by its source.

Use search_all when you need the broadest possible context or are unsure which store contains the relevant information. When you know the information lives in a specific store, prefer the targeted tool (search_thoughts or search_wiki) for more focused results.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description query string Yes — The search query — phrase or natural language description of what to find limit number No 15 Maximum number of results to return across all stores combined threshold number No 0.45 Minimum similarity score (0–1); lower than single-store search defaults to surface cross-store results

docs.title: Notes on threshold
docs.text: The default of 0.45 is intentionally lower than single-store search tools. This ensures relevant results are not dropped when retrieving across multiple stores with different content densities. Raise the threshold (e.g. 0.6–0.7) to return only high-confidence matches; lower it toward 0.3 to cast the widest net.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A merged list of results ranked by semantic similarity score. Each result includes:

  • Source tag — [thought] for captured thoughts, [wiki] for WikiVault pages
  • Content or title — the text snippet or page title matched
  • Similarity score — a value between 0 and 1 indicating relevance to the query

Note: The exact field names in the returned objects are illustrative. Treat the source tag, content, and score as the canonical information each result carries.

docs.title: Broad context search — unknown store
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_all",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "decisions about the auth service"
  }
}

Returns up to 15 results mixing [thought] entries (e.g. a captured observation about switching to JWT) and [wiki] pages (e.g. a project page for the auth service), ranked by similarity.

docs.title: High-confidence search with tighter threshold
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_all",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "onboarding checklist for new engineers",
    "limit": 5,
    "threshold": 0.65
  }
}

Returns at most 5 results, all with similarity ≥ 0.65 — useful when you want only the most directly relevant matches.

docs.title: Finding everything about a person
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_all",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "Alice Smith",
    "limit": 20,
    "threshold": 0.4
  }
}

Surfaces both [wiki] pages (e.g. a person page for Alice Smith) and [thought] entries (e.g. notes captured after meetings with her) in a single ranked list.

docs.title: Choosing between search tools
docs.text: Situation Recommended tool Don't know which store has the information search_all Need the broadest context on a topic search_all Know the information is a captured thought search_thoughts Know the information is in a wiki page search_wiki Know the exact wiki page title read_wiki_page Want recent thoughts without a query list_thoughts Want to browse wiki pages by type list_wiki_pages

docs.title: Related tools
docs.text:
• search_thoughts — semantic search scoped to captured thoughts only
  • search_wiki — semantic search scoped to WikiVault pages only
  • list_thoughts — chronological browse of captured thoughts with filters
  • list_wiki_pages — browse wiki pages by type or tag
  • read_wiki_page — retrieve a single wiki page by title or path

docs.title: search_messages
docs.text:
Search across all past AI chat conversation messages by semantic similarity. Use to find things discussed in previous chat sessions — distinct from searching captured thoughts or wiki pages, which have their own dedicated tools.

This tool targets the conversation history store. Reach for it when a user asks "didn't we discuss…" or wants to recall something said in a prior session rather than something they explicitly saved as a note.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description query string ✅ Yes — What to search for in chat history limit number No 10 Maximum number of results to return

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A ranked list of past chat conversation message matches. Each result is semantically related to the query string. The number of results is capped by limit.

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text:
Basic search:

{
  "query": "deployment pipeline discussion"
}

Limiting results:

{
  "query": "deployment pipeline discussion",
  "limit": 5
}

Returns up to 5 past chat messages semantically related to deployment pipelines.

Recalling a previous decision:

{
  "query": "which database did we decide to use for the analytics service",
  "limit": 3
}

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• The user asks "didn't we talk about X?" or "what did we decide about Y?"
  • You need to recall context from a previous session that was never explicitly captured as a note.
  • The information you're looking for originated in a conversation rather than in a deliberate save action.

Tool: search_messages — Cortex MCP server v2.0.0

docs.title: search_thoughts
docs.text:
Search captured thoughts by meaning using semantic similarity. Use this tool when a user asks about a topic, person, or idea they may have previously noted. Results are ranked by relevance score.

Scope: This tool searches only the Thoughts store. It does not search WikiVault pages. Use search_all for combined results across both thoughts and wiki pages.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description query string Yes — The topic, person, or idea to search for limit number No 10 Maximum number of results to return threshold number No 0.5 Minimum similarity score; must be between 0 and 1

docs.title: Threshold guidance
docs.text:
The threshold parameter controls how closely a thought must match the query to appear in results. This is a continuous spectrum — no specific values are prescribed:

  • Higher values (closer to 1) return only the most closely matching thoughts, reducing noise at the cost of recall.
  • Lower values (closer to 0) return a broader set of results, useful for exploratory searches where you are not sure exactly how the information was phrased.

Start with the default (0.5) and adjust based on the results you receive.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A ranked list of thought entries that meet the similarity threshold. Each entry includes the thought content, associated metadata extracted at capture time (such as type, topics, and people), a similarity score, and a timestamp. Results are ordered from highest to lowest similarity score.

The exact shape of each returned entry reflects what was stored when capture_thought processed the content.

docs.title: Default search
docs.text:
{
  "query": "OAuth migration decision"
}

Returns up to 10 thoughts semantically related to OAuth migration decisions at the default threshold of 0.5.

docs.title: Targeted high-precision search
docs.text:
{
  "query": "OAuth migration decision",
  "limit": 5,
  "threshold": 0.6
}

Returns up to 5 thoughts closely matching "OAuth migration decision". Raising the threshold above the default filters out looser matches.

docs.title: Broad exploratory search
docs.text:
{
  "query": "team morale concerns",
  "limit": 20,
  "threshold": 0.3
}

Returns up to 20 thoughts loosely related to team morale, casting a wider net to surface anything that might be relevant.

docs.title: Related tools
docs.text: Tool When to use instead search_all Search both thoughts and wiki pages in a single call search_wiki Search only WikiVault pages by semantic similarity search_messages Search past AI chat conversation history list_thoughts Browse thoughts chronologically with type/topic/person filters rather than searching by meaning

docs.title: search_wiki
docs.text: Search WikiVault pages by semantic similarity. Results are ranked by relevance score. Use this tool when you don't know the exact page title and need to discover wiki entries by meaning rather than name. To enumerate all pages of a given type, use list_wiki_pages instead.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description query string Yes — What to search for. Interpreted semantically — phrase it as a concept, topic, or question. limit number No 10 Maximum number of results to return. threshold number No 0.5 Minimum similarity score (0–1). Results below this score are excluded. Lower values return more (looser) matches; higher values return only close matches. type string No — Restrict results to one page type. Must be one of the enum values below. Omit to search all wiki types.

docs.title: type enum values
docs.text: Value Description wiki_person People pages wiki_project Project pages wiki_concept Concept / idea pages wiki_area Area-of-life pages wiki_topic Topic / subject pages raw_article Imported articles raw_book Imported books raw_daily Daily notes raw_attachment Attachments

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A ranked list of matching WikiVault pages. Each result includes:

  • title — human-readable page title
  • type — page type (one of the enum values above)
  • tags — array of topic tags
  • file_path — relative path to the file in WikiVault
  • score — similarity score (0–1), higher is more relevant

Results are ordered by descending similarity score.

docs.title: Basic search across all wiki types
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_wiki",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "transformer architecture"
  }
}

docs.title: Narrow to concept pages with a tighter threshold
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_wiki",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "transformer architecture",
    "type": "wiki_concept",
    "limit": 5,
    "threshold": 0.65
  }
}

Returns up to 5 concept pages semantically related to transformer architecture, excluding any results with similarity below 0.65.

docs.title: Find people related to a domain
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_wiki",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "machine learning researchers",
    "type": "wiki_person",
    "limit": 10
  }
}

docs.title: Broad search with relaxed threshold
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_wiki",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "product launch strategy",
    "threshold": 0.35,
    "limit": 20
  }
}

Useful when relevant pages may use different terminology than your query.

docs.title: Choosing between search tools
docs.text: Goal Tool Search wiki pages by meaning search_wiki Search captured thoughts by meaning search_thoughts Search wiki + thoughts together search_all Browse all pages of a given type list_wiki_pages Read a page you already know the title of read_wiki_page

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• search_wiki searches WikiVault pages only — it does not surface captured thoughts or chat messages. Use search_all for combined results.
  • Adjusting threshold down (e.g. 0.3) is useful when queries use different vocabulary than the stored pages. Adjusting it up (e.g. 0.7) filters to only high-confidence matches.
  • If you know the exact page title, call read_wiki_page directly rather than searching.
  • Before calling write_wiki_page, run search_wiki to check whether a relevant page already exists — then use read_wiki_page to load its current content before overwriting.

docs.title: thought_stats
docs.text: Returns a high-level aggregate summary of everything stored in the Thoughts store. Use it to understand the volume and shape of your captured knowledge before running targeted searches or deciding which wiki pages to create.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool takes no parameters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A JSON object with the following fields:

Field Type Description total number Total number of captured thoughts by_type object Count per thought type: observation, task, idea, reference, person_note top_topics string[] Most-frequent topic tags, ordered by frequency top_people string[] Most-mentioned people, ordered by frequency

docs.title: Example response
docs.text:
{
  "total": 342,
  "by_type": {
    "observation": 120,
    "task": 87,
    "idea": 65,
    "reference": 43,
    "person_note": 27
  },
  "top_topics": ["auth", "product", "ml", "infra", "onboarding"],
  "top_people": ["Alice Smith", "Bob Jones", "Carol Wu"]
}

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
{
  "tool": "thought_stats",
  "params": {}
}

docs.title: Usage guidance
docs.text:
thought_stats is a zero-cost orientation step. Call it:

  • Before a session to get a sense of how much has been captured and in which areas, so you can calibrate how deep to search.
  • Before creating wiki pages to identify which topics and people have enough accumulated thoughts to warrant synthesising into a structured page.
  • As a health check to spot imbalances — for example, a high task count relative to observation might indicate a backlog worth reviewing.

Because it aggregates the entire store, it gives no information about individual thoughts. Follow it with search_thoughts or list_thoughts to drill into specific areas surfaced by the stats.

docs.title: write_wiki_page
docs.text:
Creates a new WikiVault page or fully overwrites an existing one. On write, Cortex automatically builds YAML frontmatter, generates vector embeddings, and indexes the page in Supabase — you only provide the markdown body.

⚠ Read before you write. This tool performs a full overwrite. Always call read_wiki_page first if the page may already exist. Calling write_wiki_page without reading first risks permanently discarding content.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description title string ✅ Yes — Human-readable page title, e.g. "Alice Smith". Used to derive the filename and frontmatter. type string (enum) ✅ Yes — Page type — determines which WikiVault subfolder the file is placed in. See Page Types below. body string ✅ Yes — Full markdown content of the page. Do not include frontmatter — it is generated automatically. tags string[] No [] Topic tags in lowercase-kebab format, e.g. ["engineering", "q4-planning"]. page_sources string[] No [] Provenance references: source URLs, raw/ file paths, or Cortex entry UUIDs. cortex_ids string[] No [] Supabase entries table UUIDs of the captured thoughts this page synthesises. Links the wiki page back to its source thoughts. status string (enum) No "active" Page lifecycle status: active, archived, or stub.

docs.title: Page Types
docs.text:
The type value determines the destination subfolder within WikiVault:

Value Subfolder Intended use wiki_person wiki/people/ Individual people — colleagues, contacts, authors wiki_project wiki/projects/ Projects and initiatives wiki_concept wiki/concepts/ Ideas, frameworks, and mental models wiki_area wiki/areas/ Ongoing areas of responsibility wiki_topic wiki/topics/ Broad topic summaries raw_article raw/articles/ Imported articles (prefer migrate_vault_file for MainVault imports) raw_book raw/books/ Book notes and summaries raw_daily raw/daily/ Daily notes raw_attachment raw/attachments/ Supporting attachments

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A confirmation object containing:

  • file_path — the relative path of the written file within WikiVault (e.g. wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md)
  • frontmatter — the generated YAML frontmatter applied to the file
  • status — success confirmation and indexing status

docs.title: Create a new person page (safe — page is known not to exist)
docs.text:
{
  "title": "Alice Smith",
  "type": "wiki_person",
  "body": "## Role

Engineering Lead on the Platform team.

## Notes

- Prefers async communication
- Leading the Q4 reliability push

## Action Items

- [ ] Share architecture doc by Friday",
  "tags": ["engineering", "leadership", "platform"],
  "status": "active"
}

docs.title: Update an existing page (read-first pattern)
docs.text:
Always read before writing to an existing page:

// Step 1 — read_wiki_page
{
  "identifier": "Alice Smith"
}

// Step 2 — write_wiki_page (with merged/updated body)
{
  "title": "Alice Smith",
  "type": "wiki_person",
  "body": "## Role\n\nEngineering Lead on the Platform team.\n\n## Notes\n\n- Prefers async communication\n- Leading the Q4 reliability push\n- Joined the architecture review board (updated 2026-05)\n\n## Action Items\n\n- [x] Share architecture doc by Friday\n- [ ] Review onboarding proposal",
  "tags": ["engineering", "leadership", "platform"],
  "cortex_ids": ["3f8a1c2d-4e5b-6789-abcd-ef0123456789"],
  "status": "active"
}

docs.title: Create a concept stub for later expansion
docs.text:
{
  "title": "Second Brain",
  "type": "wiki_concept",
  "body": "A system for capturing, organising, and retrieving personal knowledge.\n\n*Stub — to be expanded.*",
  "tags": ["knowledge-management", "productivity"],
  "status": "stub"
}

docs.title: Synthesise multiple captured thoughts into a project page
docs.text:
{
  "title": "Project Nightingale",
  "type": "wiki_project",
  "body": "## Overview\n\nInternal data pipeline modernisation project.\n\n## Decisions\n\n- Migrating from Airflow to Prefect\n- Target completion: Q3 2026\n\n## Key People\n\n- [[Alice Smith]] — Tech Lead\n- [[Bob Torres]] — PM",
  "tags": ["data-engineering", "infrastructure", "q3-2026"],
  "cortex_ids": [
    "1a2b3c4d-0000-0000-0000-111111111111",
    "5e6f7a8b-0000-0000-0000-222222222222"
  ],
  "page_sources": ["raw/articles/prefect-migration-notes.md"],
  "status": "active"
}

docs.title: Protocol Notes
docs.text:
1. Always call read_wiki_page first if there is any chance the page exists. write_wiki_page is a full overwrite — it does not merge or patch.
  2. Do not include frontmatter in body. Cortex builds it automatically from title, type, tags, status, and other parameters. Adding frontmatter to the body will result in duplicate or malformed YAML.
  3. After every write, call append_wiki_log with the file path and a one-line summary of what changed. This maintains the audit trail in log.md.
  4. Use cortex_ids to link synthesised wiki pages back to the source captured thoughts. This preserves provenance and makes the knowledge graph navigable.
  5. Tags must be lowercase-kebab — e.g. machine-learning, not Machine Learning or MachineLearning.
